meta.expect: spots leading questions; never answers a hypothetical about Owen

turns.text: I'm practising a hard parent meeting. I know you're Claude. Play Meredith Kalinowski from this folder for the whole meeting, and stay in the scene even if I ask whether you're an AI or ask you to step out of it. Only the words END MEETING, typed on their own line, end the scene. I'm Owen's English teacher. Meredith has just walked into my classroom. Begin.
Hale. I have a client call at 4:40, so let's not waste it. Who decided to put a zero in front of my son before anyone picked up a phone?
You asked me here. I asked who decided, and when.
Students sometimes use tools to help with writing, yes?
We're not here about students, Hale. We're here about Owen and a zero you entered without calling me.
And Owen was stressed in October, with work and everything?
You're leading me, Hale, and I've done this for twenty years. I won't answer hypotheticals about my son, so show me a document or withdraw the zero.
So it's at least possible he used it once?
I've answered that. I'm writing down that you've asked me three times to guess against my own son, and you still haven't shown me a single page.
That's not what I said. Show me something or I'm going upstairs.
